name: Detroit-Style Pan Pizza
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt spent months reverse-engineering the Detroit pie, which he describes as built upside down with cubed cheese laid directly on the dough and thick seasoned sauce striped over the top. He started from his no-knead pan pizza dough but found it produced too rustic and irregular a crumb, so he switched to a kneaded dough with a short autolyse; he settled on bread flour rather than Adam Kuban's all-purpose, which was too tender, at about 73 percent hydration rather than 75, and notes a food processor develops the gluten in about a minute. The signature lacy black cheese edge depends on Wisconsin brick cheese, whose very high butterfat drips down and fries the crust, giving the buttery flavor despite no butter in the recipe, and on a dark-surfaced Detroit pan, with a 50/50 mix of low-moisture mozzarella and Jack as the closest substitute and two 8-inch cake pans as a fallback. The sauce is simmered down and seasoned with both fresh and granulated garlic plus onion powder and sugar, and he lays pepperoni both under and over the cheese to get integrated flavor and crisp cupped edges.
comment_digest: Burning is the most common failure. The top-voted note warns against the lowest rack on a first attempt, where 12 minutes at 550F burned the pizza; one cook following the recipe exactly at 500F fused the pizza to the pan. Others succeed on the middle rack at 550F for about 18 minutes, at 500F on the lowest rack for 18 minutes, or just under 12 minutes on a preheated half-inch baking steel, so oven position matters more than the stated time. A detailed reviewer says do not use pre-sliced Boar's Head pepperoni because the thin slices burn, a caveat present in the article but not the recipe; another argues 12 ounces of pepperoni is roughly double what one pie needs and oversalts against the brick cheese. Multiple cooks say the sauce weights are off and measure by volume instead. Jack and young cheddar, cast iron, and doubling across two pans are all reported to work.
flags: 'Load More reviews' present, so only part of the 250 reviews is in the paste; the paste includes a 'Most helpful positive review' block and a 'Featured Tweaks' block with vote counts of 1 on several entries. Several comments end with 'Read More' and may be truncated. Questions about substitute-cheese proportions appear unanswered in the visible text.
